sentences.text: Scientists currently recognize seven different species within the genus Protolamna.
This genus holds the title of the oldest-known gigantic lamniform shark.
Fossil evidence suggests that gigantism evolved very early in the history of this shark group.
Researchers have documented 82 separate fossil occurrences of Protolamna in the Paleobiology Database.
The animal is classified in the class Chondrichthyes, which includes all cartilaginous fish.
It belongs to the family Pseudoscapanorhynchidae, a group that serves as its parent classification.
The genus was formally described by Cappetta in 1985, with Protolamna sokolovi serving as the type species.
Protolamna lived from the Valanginian to the Maastrichtian, spanning from 137.05 to 66 million years ago.
